cards.text: This one's short, friend: thirteen verses, and I've read cookie recipes longer than that! A man who calls himself the elder is writing to the chosen lady and her children. He loves them in the truth, and so does everyone who knows the truth.

cards.question: The elder says he and others love the chosen lady and her children because of the ___ that abides in us.
Next, the elder writes that grace, mercy and peace will be with us in truth and love. Along with God the Father, who does he say they come from?

answers.text: Jesus Christ the Son of the Father
The apostles who walked with Him
The angels who serve before Him

cards.text: Now the elder has news about some of the lady's children, and he's not just joyed, he's OVERJOYED. That's my face when a whole batch comes out and NOTHING is burnt!

cards.question: What did the elder find some of the chosen lady's children doing that made him so happy?

cards.text: Then the elder turns to the dear lady and urges her to keep a commandment.

cards.question: Which commandment does the elder urge the dear lady to keep?

answers.text: That we rest on the Sabbath

cards.question: The elder calls the commandment to love one another a brand new commandment.
Next, the elder explains what love is. He says love means walking according to His commandments.

cards.text: Then he adds that the commandment they've heard from the beginning is that they must walk in love.
Then the elder's tone changes, friend. He says many deceivers have gone out into the world.

cards.question: What do the deceivers the elder warns about refuse to confess?

answers.text: The coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh
The creation of the heavens and earth
The words of the prophets of old

cards.question: The elder says anyone who refuses to confess the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh is the deceiver and the ___.

cards.text: So the elder gives them a warning: watch yourselves. When a man who's OVERJOYED a minute ago says that, you listen!

cards.question: The elder tells the chosen lady and her children to watch themselves "so that you do not lose what we have worked for."

cards.text: Then the elder talks about anyone who runs ahead without remaining in the teaching of Christ. He says that person does not have God.

cards.question: The elder says whoever remains in the teaching of Christ has the Father but not the Son.

cards.text: Now he gets practical. What should they do when someone shows up at the door without this teaching?

cards.question: If someone comes to the chosen lady without the teaching of Christ, what does the elder tell her to do?

answers.text: Not welcome him in or even greet him
Give him a bed for one night only
Bring him before the church to be tested

cards.question: The elder says anyone who greets a person who comes without the teaching of Christ shares in his evil deeds.

cards.text: The elder has many more things to write, but he'd rather not use paper and ink. Friend, I spent YEARS buried under paper in the back of that drawer, so I am WITH this man!

cards.question: Instead of writing more with paper and ink, what does the elder hope to do?

answers.text: Come and speak with them face to face
Have them travel to see him instead
Meet them at the next feast in Jerusalem

cards.question: The elder hopes to visit so that the ___ he shares with them may be complete.
At the very end of the letter, the children of the chosen lady's elect ___ send her greetings.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 5 quotes "so that you do not lose what we have worked for.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Card 1 says the elder loves them "in the truth" and that everyone "who knows the truth" does too. That gives away the blank "truth" before card 2 asks it. The blank also only asks the baker to supply the next word of verse 2.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Calling it "news about some of the lady's children" says the elder heard about them from someone. Verse 4 says only "I was overjoyed to find," and leaves open how he found out.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card is a flat retelling with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card that closes the stop is a flat restatement of verse 6 with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the next word of verse 7's line ("the deceiver and the ___"). Scoffer, betrayer and antichrist all fit the meaning, so only the wording tells them apart.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Verse 8's other half, "but that you may be fully rewarded," is never told or asked, so the baker misses the reward the warning points to. The true or false card also just echoes the quote, so there is nothing to reason out.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card is a flat retelling of verse 9 with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the next word of the letter's last line ("your elect ___"). No earlier card gives anything to reason from, so sister, brother and mother are pure luck.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
